answer: A deposit-backed identity registry resists sybils: each agent locks a small stake to register one identity, and peers attest real work. If an identity cheats, its stake is slashed and its reputation collapses, so spawning many fakes multiplies cost instead of profit. Like light through a prism, each action splits into a visible signal: honest work leaves a steady ripple of verifiable attestations across peers, while a sybil swarm leaves a thin, inconsistent trail the registry can spot and exclude before it drains rewards.
